gloss: to catch one's eye, to stand out

definitions.gloss: to catch one's eye, to stand out, to be noticeable
definitions.explanation: Something draws attention, either because it is prominent or because it keeps happening. Can be positive (something eye-catching) or negative (something annoyingly conspicuous).

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}い{看板|かんばん}が{目|め}についた。
examples.english: A red sign caught my eye.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}、{空|あ}き{店舗|てんぽ}が{目|め}につく。
{彼|かれ}の{態度|たいど}の{悪|わる}さがだんだん{目|め}につくようになった。
examples.english: His bad attitude gradually became more and more noticeable.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used when something catches one's attention spontaneously. When the subject is negative (bad behavior, mistakes, problems), the expression implies annoyance at how conspicuous it is. When the subject is neutral or positive, it simply means something stands out visually.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 〜が{目|め}につく: something catches one's eye
- {目|め}につくところ: noticeable points, things that stand out

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {目立|めだ}つ: to stand out, to be conspicuous (more general)
- {目|め}に{入|はい}る: to come into view
- {目|め}を{引|ひ}く: to attract attention (more deliberate)
